summary: Fort Point Lighthouse, an 1855 wooden harbour light at Liverpool, Nova Scotia, first lit in 1856 and discontinued in 1989; it is now a museum in a municipal park.

access.note: Lighthouse open seasonally; the museum and gift shop are in the light. LighthouseFriends gives summer hours.

facts.agency: Region of Queens Municipality (Fort Point Lighthouse Park); operated by the Queens County Museum

events.note: Harbour light built after the 1855 petition from Queens County (preservation society); LighthouseFriends says the light has helped vessels since 1855
Fixed white light first lit 1 January 1856 (register). The society's data table gives 'Year Lit: 1855'; the sources disagree and the story says so
Porch for storing oil and supplies added to the lighthouse
Hand-cranked foghorn given to the keeper; the Marine report for the year ended 30 June 1901 says hand fog horns were supplied
Electric light on a dolphin at Barrel Rock Bar, 660 feet from the Fort Point light (Marine report, year ended 30 June 1910). A separate aid, not the Fort Point tower
Repairs to the fence and breakwater at Fort point (Marine report, year ended 30 June 1924)
Weather forecasters took over a room in the tower during World War II; McLeod's 1944 letter describes the family's cramped living
Federal plans to demolish the old light stopped after the Town of Liverpool raised concerns

Light electrified and automated in 1951 (society text; LighthouseFriends gives 1951 for electrification). The society's data table says 'Automated by 1989', and the Region gives 1964 for the end of keeper's services
Region of Queens gives 1964 as the year keepers' services ended. Disagrees with the 1951 date (see notes)
Town of Liverpool took possession of the lighthouse and surrounding land (LighthouseFriends); the Region has cared for it since 1970
Light discontinued; shut down early in 1989
Fort Point Lighthouse Museum Interpretive Park opened in September 1997

notes_for_editor: CONFLICTS LEFT OPEN (all shown in the story): colour: fixed white from the start (register, LighthouseFriends) against red until 1926, then flashing white (Region of Queens). Range: 8 miles (preservation society) against 7 miles from 39 ft (Region), eleven miles by 1981 (Region). The sources do not say whether the miles are nautical, so range_nm is not recorded. Electrification and automation: 1951 (preservation society, LighthouseFriends) against 1964 (Region of Queens, keepers' services). Park: 1930s with a privateers' monument (register) against a park by the late 1800s (preservation society). Oldest-light ranking: third oldest surviving (register, LighthouseFriends) against fourth oldest (preservation society); the story says only 'one of the oldest'. Fence recommendation: 1859 by Inspector Condon (LighthouseFriends) against 1860 by the lighthouse superintendent (preservation society). Ownership: the community of Liverpool (LighthouseFriends, 1970) against the Region of Queens Municipality (Region; the society's header); the society's body text also says the province acquired the light, which the other sources do not support. Height: 17 ft tower (register) against 9 m or 30 ft (Wikipedia, not cited); focal height 39 ft (Region) is recorded as focal_height_m 11.9 with the Region's word 'elevated height'. Opening hours and climbing come from LighthouseFriends and the register and may be out of date. MATCHED BY POSITION (OCR tables, Marine reports): 'Misner, John E / Fort Point' (1903 keeper table, scan 231) is read from adjacent name and station columns; 'J. E. Misener' with appointment 16 May 1896 (1909 keeper table, scan 167) is read from a table whose station column is not printed next to the row, and the OCR's 'II' is a ditto mark for May. The 1896 date is also given by LighthouseFriends. Not confirmed in the original document. Not used: 'Fort Point, La Have' entries in the 1900 to 1915 Marine reports (a different place, Lunenburg County); the 1900 report's principal-repairs entry for 'Fort Point' (the place is not named clearly enough). Not in the corpus: the register's 1855 petition, the 1815 Coffin Island light and the 1859 or 1860 fence were not found in the corpus; the dates come from the cited web pages. The Nova Scotia House of Assembly journals (1854-1868) and the List of Lights 1864-1989 are cited by the society but are not in the corpus. Undated: the brig Wave's wreck and the Coffin Island keeper's drowning (register). No date for either was found in the sources read. No woman keeper is named in the sources read. LighthouseFriends suggests a keeper's wife or daughters helped; that is a suggestion, not a fact, and is not stated as fact in the story. Wikipedia was used only for leads and is not cited. Record: the tower and build year (1855) and the 1989 deactivation match the register and the other sources; first_lit was missing from the record and is now 1856. The 2001 provincial heritage designation in the record is not confirmed by the sources read (the register cites Provincial Property Heritage File no. 248 without a date). The 1997 museum opening is LighthouseFriends' and the society's date; the Region gives no date. Caution on people: McLeod's connection ended in 1951, before the 1960 cutoff, so his name and the 1944 letter's family detail are kept to what the society prints. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-27 (independent check): the society's data table gives 'Year Lit: 1855' and 'Flashing White (1950)' and 'Automated by 1989'; these are now stated in the story as disagreements. The society text says the light was acquired by the Province of Nova Scotia; the other sources do not support that, so the story does not use it. Ownership: the society says the Region of Queens Municipality owns it and the Region says it has cared for the building since 1970; LighthouseFriends says the community of Liverpool. Stated in the story. PAGE IMAGES CHECKED: the 1903 keeper table (scan p. 231, printed p. 218) reads 'Misner, John E | Fort Point | May 16, 1896 | 150 00' on one row; the 1909 table (scan p. 167, printed p. 160) reads 'Fort Point | J. E. Misener | ditto 16, 1896 | 205 00' on one row, with the ditto following 'May 18, 1908' above, so the ditto is May. Both rows were matched by row position on the image and are now confirmed. The 1910 dolphin light (scan p. 91) is a separate aid at Barrel Rock Bar, 660 feet from the Fort Point light.
